rollback_evidence: 1.0.12 switch ip routing (X39), measured on EXOS-VM 33.6.1.14 in the virtual topology. Key: <vlan>:<vrid> (VRID 1-255, the VLAN name as configured). Create: 'create vrrp vlan V vrid N', 'configure vrrp vlan V vrid N priority P' (100 is the default and not printed), 'configure vrrp vlan V vrid N add VIP', 'enable vrrp vlan V vrid N' unless admin-state is disabled (the per-instance form; the global 'enable vrrp' would enable every instance). Update: priority, a new virtual address is added before the old one is deleted, enable/disable. Delete: 'delete vrrp vlan V vrid N' removes the instance with its address, priority and state. One IPv4 virtual address; a second address, IPv6, tracking, timers, preempt, accept mode, version or authentication lines are outside the profile and refused. An instance without a virtual address (create vrrp vlan V vrid N alone, measured) is read with its priority and state; its priority is changed and it is deleted or recreated without an address, but it is not enabled (the switch refuses: 'VR must have at least 1 virtual IP address!') and a first address is not added to it (its return is not measured). Refused before any write: Default, Mgmt and protected VLANs, a VLAN with a protected member port (protected.ports and the audit policy protected_ports), a VLAN without an IPv4 address, a virtual address outside its subnet or equal to the VLAN address (address owner, priority 255). A VLAN with VRRP is referenced and is not deleted, and its IPv4 address is not changed. The check account reads show vrrp vlan V and show vrrp (rows equal to the total) for an absent instance.
